dependsOn: AuthService — OAuth2 token validation and certificate-based client auth
BlobStorageService — file uploads for bulk import/export

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic User aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: User.cs contains only setter-level format guards (not-null, ShortGuid format check). All real business invariants — username and ssoId uniqueness (DefaultUserService.cs:752–758), XSS sanitisation of Organization/FirstName/LastName (lines 736–744), audit-field stamping, password initialisation, and custom-property defaulting (lines 614–690) — live in DefaultUserService. A DDD aggregate must protect its own consistency boundary without relying on the service layer to enforce rules.

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic Group aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: Group.cs is a pure data bag with no methods. Invariants — name uniqueness per tenant, Everyone-group mutation prevention, Smart-group rule validation — all live in GroupService (lines 90–160) and DefaultSmartGroupService. GroupService.CreateUserGroupAsync calls a repository to check uniqueness, then throws, with no participation from Group itself; the aggregate cannot protect its consistency in any other code path.

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic User aggregate — 99K-line service
gapAnalysis.detail: User.cs contains only data properties and no domain methods. All business rules (activation guards, group membership validation, duplicate detection, cache eviction) live in DefaultUserService.cs (~99K lines). For example, the invariant 'a deactivated user cannot be added to a group' is enforced by a guard clause in DefaultUserService.AddUserToGroupAsync, not by User.AssignToGroup(). Any future change to this invariant requires navigating the service monolith. The fix is to move invariant-enforcing methods onto User itself, reducing DefaultUserService to an orchestrator that calls aggregate methods and publishes events.

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic Group aggregate — 38K-line service
gapAnalysis.detail: Group.cs is a data bag. GroupService.cs (~39K lines) contains all membership management, owner validation, and type-specific constraints (e.g., Everyone group is singleton, Smart groups cannot have direct members). The constraint 'Everyone group cannot have members added manually' is a service-layer if-check rather than an invariant on the Group aggregate. Moving type-specific behaviour into a GroupType strategy or into Group.AddMember()/Group.Create() would make violations impossible by construction.

gapAnalysis.title: Kafka event publishing in domain service layer
gapAnalysis.detail: UmsEventBus.PublishAsync() is called directly from DefaultUserService and GroupService after persistence operations. This couples domain logic to Kafka infrastructure: the service must know about topics, Avro serialisation, and delivery semantics. If Kafka is unavailable the business operation fails. The pattern should be: aggregate raises an in-process domain event → a post-commit dispatcher reads pending events and publishes to Kafka. This decouples the domain from the transport and enables reliable outbox patterns.

gapAnalysis.title: Dual aggregate write in group membership — consistency gap
gapAnalysis.detail: When a user is added to a group, both Group.DirectGroupIds (logically the group's member list) and User.DirectGroupIds (the user's group list) are updated in the same service method across two repository calls without a unit-of-work boundary. If the second write fails, the aggregate pair is inconsistent. One of these lists should be the single source of truth (the join table in SQL) and the other derived, or both writes should be wrapped in a transaction/outbox.

gapAnalysis.title: DefaultUserService god object — 16 dependencies
gapAnalysis.detail: DefaultUserService constructor takes 16 injected dependencies (IGroupRepository, IUserRepository, IUserIdentifyValidator, ICustomPropertyService, IDataSchemaService, ICustomPropertyVerifyService, ILibraryCacheNotitionSevice, IRequestContext, IUmsEventBus, ILogger, UmsDeployInfo, IUserCacheService, IHttpContextAccessor, IUserPostChangeProcessor, IGroupInterceptor, IGroupMemberEventService) and spans ~2,200 lines. It mixes CRUD, validation, cache management, event publishing, HTTP context inspection, and feature flag evaluation in a single class.

gapAnalysis.title: Infrastructure calls directly in BulkController
gapAnalysis.detail: BulkController injects IBlobStorageService and IJobManagementService and calls them directly in action methods: UploadAsync calls BlobStorageService.UploadAsync(), GetDownloadFileAsync calls BlobStorageService.GetDownloadUrlAsync(), GetExceptionDownloadFileAsync calls BlobStorageService.UploadAsync() and writes CSV bytes inline. Controllers should delegate to application services; infrastructure must not be called from the HTTP layer.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain events modelled as Kafka infrastructure events
gapAnalysis.detail: UserEvent, GroupEvent, GroupMemberEvent, and UserCustomPropertyEvent are Avro-serialised Kafka message classes living in the infrastructure layer. There is no domain event abstraction (e.g. IDomainEvent). Business logic raises events by calling IUmsEventBus directly rather than appending to an aggregate's domain event list, coupling the domain layer to the messaging infrastructure.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain events fired from service, not aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: Events are constructed and dispatched directly in service method bodies: DefaultUserService.cs:680 (_umsEventBus.SendUserEvent), GroupService.cs:106 (_umsEventBus.SendGroupEvent). Aggregates have no Raise() mechanism, so any code path that bypasses the service layer can silently omit events. This also couples the service to Kafka infrastructure rather than to a domain event abstraction.

gapAnalysis.title: SmartGroup rule logic not encapsulated in a distinct aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: SmartGroup has a rich rule language (Rule.cs, SmartGroupUnit.cs, per-field operator validators in RuleFields/, SmartGroupRuleSetListValidationHelper) but reuses the flat Group aggregate with a GroupType.Smart discriminator. Rule invariants such as valid operator-field combinations and rule-set depth constraints are validated in DefaultSmartGroupService rather than enforced by a SmartGroup aggregate that expresses these as first-class business rules.

gapAnalysis.title: UserService has cross-domain knowledge of GroupMemberEvent
gapAnalysis.detail: DefaultUserService injects IGroupMemberEventService and calls it directly during membership operations (DefaultUserService.cs:513 and 601). The User Identity domain should not know how to construct or publish Group-domain events; this coupling means a change to GroupMemberEvent structure forces changes inside DefaultUserService.

gapAnalysis.title: UserSyncConfig stores opaque JToken blobs instead of typed value objects
gapAnalysis.detail: UserSyncConfig.ExternalAuthentication and SyncProperties are JToken fields — opaque JSON blobs at the type-system level. Business constraints on valid sync configuration are invisible to the compiler. Additionally, AesCryptor is instantiated ad-hoc in UserSyncConfigService instead of being injected, coupling the domain service to a concrete infrastructure class.

gapAnalysis.title: No in-process domain events — post-persist side effects are invisible
gapAnalysis.detail: Domain events (UserCreated, GroupMemberAdded) are produced only as Kafka messages after persistence. There is no in-process IEventDispatcher or domain event collection on aggregates. This means side effects (welcome email, smart group recompute, V1–V2 sync) cannot be triggered synchronously in tests without a running Kafka broker. Introducing a DomainEvent base class and collecting events on the aggregate before dispatch would allow all consumers to be tested in-process.

gapAnalysis.title: SCIM PatchOp translation in controller layer
gapAnalysis.detail: SCIMUsersController and SCIMGroupsController translate SCIM PATCH operations (RFC 7644 §3.5.2 op/value/path semantics) into internal model mutations inline in the controller action. This is protocol logic that belongs in an anti-corruption layer (SCIMAdapter or SCIMPatchTranslator service) that maps SCIM concepts to domain commands, keeping the controller a thin HTTP boundary.

gapAnalysis.title: Value objects missing — UserType, TenantId, ShortGuid as primitives
gapAnalysis.detail: UserType is used as an enum but validation (e.g., 'Partner users cannot have Premium features') is scattered across service checks. TenantId is a raw string/Guid passed into every method instead of being a typed value object that could carry its own validation. ShortGuid is converted ad-hoc throughout. Introducing UserType, TenantId, and ShortGuid value objects with self-validating constructors would eliminate an entire class of invalid-argument bugs and make method signatures self-documenting.

gapAnalysis.title: Specification pattern absent — SmartGroup rule evaluation coupled to persistence
gapAnalysis.detail: DefaultSmartGroupService.cs builds raw SQL/EF predicates from Rule objects rather than using a composable Specification pattern. The partial RuleSet/Rule value objects exist but do not implement ISpecification<User>. Adding a UserSpecificationBuilder that converts a RuleSet to an IQueryable<User> predicate would isolate query construction, make individual rules unit-testable in memory, and allow smart group evaluation to run without a DB in tests.

gapAnalysis.title: GroupService god object — 14 dependencies
gapAnalysis.detail: GroupService constructor takes 14 injected dependencies and directly calls ICacheService.InvalidateAsync(), IUmsEventBus.SendGroupEvent(), IGroupRepository, and IGroupV2OwnerRepository inside business methods. Validation, persistence, caching, and event publishing are collapsed into a single service.

gapAnalysis.title: SCIM layer bypasses User/Group domain layer
gapAnalysis.detail: SCIMUsersController injects IScimUserService and ISCIMGroupService which make direct repository calls rather than routing through DefaultUserService and GroupService. This means SCIM provisioning bypasses domain invariants (e.g. SSO-ID uniqueness, EveryoneGroup protection) enforced only in the core services.

gapAnalysis.title: LaunchDarkly feature flag evaluated inside domain service
gapAnalysis.detail: DefaultUserService calls LaunchDarklyHelper.EnableRepoV2() inside business methods to choose between LibraryUser and LibraryUserV2 repositories. Feature flag infrastructure does not belong in the domain layer; this should be resolved at the application or composition root layer before reaching the service.

gapAnalysis.title: BulkJobService is a thin JMS wrapper with no domain logic
gapAnalysis.detail: BulkJobService contains two lines of logic per method — all delegating directly to IJobManagementService. The BulkJob lifecycle (Queued → Processing → Completed/Failed/Cancelled) has no aggregate representation; state transitions are entirely implicit in JMS.

gapAnalysis.title: HTTP context inspected inside DefaultUserService
gapAnalysis.detail: DefaultUserService accesses IHttpContextAccessor.HttpContext.Request.Headers inside business methods to extract caller context. Domain services must not depend on HTTP infrastructure; caller identity should be passed as a typed parameter from the application layer.

gapAnalysis.title: V1/V2 dual-write complexity with bidirectional sync consumers
gapAnalysis.detail: UserEventConsumerForV1ToV2Sync and UserEventConsumerForV2ToV1Sync maintain bidirectional synchronisation between LibraryUser and LibraryUserV2. This creates a potential event loop, complicates debugging, and doubles the surface area for data inconsistency. A migration completion date and V1 deprecation plan should be established to eliminate the dual-write path.

gapAnalysis.title: Username, Email, and SsoId modelled as raw strings
gapAnalysis.detail: User identity attributes — Name (used as username), email inside UserProfileEntity, SsoId inside UserAuthSecretEntity — are raw strings. There are no Email, Username, or SsoId value objects enforcing format rules at construction time; validation is duplicated imperatively across DefaultUserService and controller validation logic.

gapAnalysis.title: UserAuthSecretEntity accessed via late-bound JToken cast
gapAnalysis.detail: Auth credentials are stored in User.Data["authSecret"] and retrieved via .ToObject<UserAuthSecretEntity>() at runtime (DefaultUserService.cs:637). This bypasses compile-time type safety, makes the sub-entity invisible to aggregate invariant checks, and means a schema change to UserAuthSecretEntity produces a runtime deserialisation failure rather than a compile error.

gapAnalysis.title: Legacy ID fields maintained alongside ShortGuid — model pollution
gapAnalysis.detail: User.DirectGroupLegacyIds, Group.OwnerUserLegacyIds, and similar *LegacyId collections coexist with ShortGuid variants across the domain model. V1–V2 sync consumers exist purely to keep these in sync at runtime. The legacy fields are an integration seam, not a domain concept, and should be isolated to an ACL/adapter layer so the domain model speaks only in ShortGuid.

gapAnalysis.title: Cache invalidation logic in domain service
gapAnalysis.detail: DefaultUserService and GroupService call IUserCacheService.InvalidateCacheAsync() and ILibraryCacheNotionService after writes. Cache management is an infrastructure concern and should not be a service-layer dependency in domain code. An event-driven cache invalidation handler (triggered by persisted domain events) would keep the domain service free of cache semantics.

gapAnalysis.title: WelcomeEmail rule logic as free functions outside aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: SmartRuleCalculationUtil.cs and WelcomeEmailRuleUtil.cs are static helper classes containing rule evaluation logic that semantically belongs to the EmailTemplate aggregate (specifically its WelcomeEmailRule value object). This makes the aggregate passively hold data while helpers perform all computation, a secondary anemic symptom in the Email Notification domain.

gapAnalysis.title: No read model for People Search — direct multi-repository fan-out
gapAnalysis.detail: CombinedSearchService and PeopleService fan out to IUserRepository and IGroupRepository directly with no CQRS read projection or materialised view. Queries cross the User and Group domain boundaries without a dedicated query model, making performance tuning and search relevance improvements difficult.

gapAnalysis.title: Repository interface fragmentation
gapAnalysis.detail: The codebase defines IUserRepository, IBulkUserRepository, IThinUserRepository, IUserCacheService, IGroupRepository, IGroupV2OwnerRepository, and more. The proliferation of narrow repository interfaces without a query specification pattern leads to duplicate method signatures and makes it hard to understand the full query surface of each aggregate.

gapAnalysis.title: Controllers return domain model objects directly
gapAnalysis.detail: Several controllers return User and Group domain objects (or collections thereof) directly via IActionResult without mapping to response DTOs. This couples the API contract to the internal domain model, making non-breaking API evolution harder and leaking internal fields (e.g. LegacyId, DirectManagedGroupLegacyIds) to external consumers.
